current_law_statement: Sessions reviewed: 2023 (long), 2024 (short), 2025 (long) and 2026 (short) — ncleg.gov General Statutes state 'The General Statutes include changes through S.L. 2026-30'; the ncleg 'Law modifications not yet reflected in statute' (2026) list shows pending changes to §§ 132-1.2(12), 132-1.3B, 132-1.4(a),(g) and 132-1.4A(b) only. Codified ch. 132 opened in full (HTML by-chapter and by-section): § 132-6.2 (fees) last amended S.L. 2004-129 s. 38 — no 2024–2026 amendment; § 132-6 current; § 132-1.4A last amended S.L. 2025-70 s. 21 (subsection (l) copy-fee text unchanged); § 132-10 last amended 1997; § 159-32.1 (electronic payment) unamended since 1999. North Carolina has no administrative-code fee schedule for public records and no uniform state schedule; the statute delegates only 'as prescribed by law' (media) and 'as provided by law' (certification), and for municipalities no such law was found. Guidance-vs-law gaps: the Attorney General's 2019 Open Government Guide (ncdoj.gov) restates the statute and adds (i) no fee for inspection, (ii) copy-employee labor generally not chargeable, (iii) special service charge cannot recover redaction/review time, (iv) postage recoverable, (v) best-practice written acknowledgment with cost information — recorded as Official Guidance; the Governor's July 2018 Cabinet-agency guidance recommends $0.05/page for printed copies and no fee for electronic production — state_agencies_only. Both guides predate the January 2025 change of AG and Governor; no later editions located. NCDOJ opinions directory searched; its 'Public Records' opinion page errored (see gaps). Municipal scope: ch. 132 binds every unit of local government; every resolution below is for municipalities with the agency regime noted where it differs.

resolutions.source_language: Except as otherwise provided by law, no public agency shall charge a fee for an uncertified copy of a public record that exceeds the actual cost to the public agency of making the copy. For purposes of this subsection, "actual cost" is limited to direct, chargeable costs related to the reproduction of a public record as determined by generally accepted accounting principles and does not include costs that would have been incurred by the public agency if a request to reproduce a public record had not been made.

resolutions.source_language: Notwithstanding the provisions of this subsection, if the request is such as to require extensive use of information technology resources or extensive clerical or supervisory assistance by personnel of the agency involved, or if producing the record in the medium requested results in a greater use of information technology resources than that established by the agency for reproduction of the volume of information requested, then the agency may charge, in addition to the actual cost of duplication, a special service charge, which shall be reasonable and shall be based on the actual cost incurred for such extensive use of information technology resources or the labor costs of the personnel providing the services, or for a greater use of information technology resources that is actually incurred by the agency or attributable to the agency. || "Actual cost" is defined as "direct, chargeable costs related to the reproduction of a public record as determined by generally accepted accounting principles." The law does not give examples of actual costs but it does say that actual cost may not include costs the agency would have incurred if the copy request had not been made. This means that under most circumstances, fees may not include the labor costs of the agency employees who make the copies. However, if making the copies involves extensive clerical or supervisory assistance, the agency may charge a special service fee in addition to actual duplication costs. This service charge must be reasonable and based on actual labor costs but cannot be charged to recover fees for time spent examining or removing confidential information from records. Agencies also may charge to recover the costs of mailing copies. Complaints or disputes about all records copying fees may be directed to the State Chief Information Officer or their designee for mediation.

new_rules.legal_concept: State policy: copies free or at minimal (actual) cost
new_rules.atomic_rule: It is State policy that the people may obtain copies of public records free or at 'minimal cost', defined as the actual cost of reproducing the record, unless otherwise specifically provided by law.
new_rules.related_rule_ids: ceiling: actual cost of reproducing the record
new_rules.is_paraphrase: Therefore, it is the policy of this State that the people may obtain copies of their public records and public information free or at minimal cost unless otherwise specifically provided by law. As used herein, "minimal cost" shall mean the actual cost of reproducing the public record or public information.
new_rules.official_link: Current (ncleg.gov current through S.L. 2026-30; § 132-1 last amended S.L. 2023-134 s. 27.7(f) and S.L. 2023-138 s. 5(b) — subsection (b) text unchanged since 1995)
new_rules.amends: 'Free' is expressly contemplated — supports discretionary no-charge decisions; no de-minimis threshold or waiver criteria attach.

new_rules.legal_concept: State CIO mediation of unfair/unreasonable copy fees
new_rules.atomic_rule: A requester charged a fee the requester believes to be unfair or unreasonable may ask the State Chief Information Officer or designee to mediate the dispute.
new_rules.trigger: Requester believes a charged fee is unfair or unreasonable
new_rules.is_paraphrase: If anyone requesting public information from any public agency is charged a fee that the requester believes to be unfair or unreasonable, the requester may ask the State Chief Information Officer or his designee to mediate the dispute.
new_rules.official_link: Current (ncleg.gov General Statutes current through S.L. 2026-30; § 132-6.2 last amended S.L. 2004-129 — no 2024, 2025 or 2026 amendment; no pending 2026 modification listed for §§ 132-6, 132-6.2, 132-1.4A(l), 132-10)
new_rules.amends: State-level fee-dispute path binding all public agencies incl. cities; mediation, not a binding order and not a fee-waiver appeal. Proposed concept key fee.dispute_mediation (no existing key fits). May duplicate pruned NC-0022.

new_rules.legal_concept: Copy fee for law-enforcement agency recordings (body-worn / dashboard camera)
new_rules.atomic_rule: A law enforcement agency may charge a fee to offset the cost incurred to make a copy of a recording for release, and the fee shall not exceed the actual cost of making the copy.
new_rules.trigger: Release of a copy of a law enforcement agency recording under § 132-1.4A
new_rules.related_rule_ids: ceiling: actual cost of making the copy
new_rules.is_paraphrase: ( l ) Fee for Copies. - A law enforcement agency may charge a fee to offset the cost incurred by it to make a copy of a recording for release. The fee shall not exceed the actual cost of making the copy.
new_rules.official_link: Current (ncleg.gov current through S.L. 2026-30; § 132-1.4A last amended S.L. 2025-70 s. 21; pending S.L. 2026-40 s. 4.53 (eff. 10/01/2026) amends subsection (b) only)
new_rules.amends: Binds municipal police departments as 'law enforcement agencies'. No per-minute rate, no free minutes. Recordings under § 132-1.4A are not public records; release generally requires a court order — the fee applies to copies made for release.

new_rules.legal_concept: GIS copies at reasonable cost; written no-resale/non-commercial-use condition
new_rules.atomic_rule: A county or city shall furnish copies of its GIS databases and data files at reasonable cost and, as a condition of furnishing an electronic copy, may require the recipient to agree in writing that the copy will not be resold or otherwise used for trade or commercial purposes (news-media publication, real-estate trade association / MLS publication or at-cost resale, and non-resale use by a licensed professional in practice are not commercial use).
new_rules.trigger: Request for copies of county/city GIS databases or data files
new_rules.is_paraphrase: Upon request, the county or city shall furnish copies, in documentary or electronic form, to anyone requesting them at reasonable cost. As a condition of furnishing an electronic copy, whether on magnetic tape, magnetic disk, compact disk, or photo-optical device, a county or city may require that the person obtaining the copy agree in writing that the copy will not be resold or otherwise used for trade or commercial purposes.
new_rules.official_link: Current (ncleg.gov current through S.L. 2026-30; § 132-10 last amended S.L. 1997-193)
new_rules.amends: The only commercial-purpose mechanism in N.C. public-records law and it is municipal/county-specific and record-specific (GIS). 'Reasonable cost' is a soft standard distinct from § 132-6.2(b) 'actual cost'. No surcharge; the condition is a written agreement, not a price.

new_rules.legal_concept: Copies furnished upon payment of lawful fees
new_rules.atomic_rule: The custodian shall, as promptly as possible, furnish copies of public records upon payment of any fees as may be prescribed by law.
new_rules.trigger: Copy request where a lawful fee applies
new_rules.is_paraphrase: Every custodian of public records shall permit any record in the custodian's custody to be inspected and examined at reasonable times and under reasonable supervision by any person, and shall, as promptly as possible, furnish copies thereof upon payment of any fees as may be prescribed by law.
new_rules.amends: Read as permitting the custodian to collect the copy fee before or at delivery ('upon payment'); no deposit, prepayment threshold, or nonpayment-withdrawal rule attaches. Inspection carries no fee condition.

new_rules.legal_concept: AG guidance: labor generally not chargeable; special service charge cannot recover redaction/review time
new_rules.atomic_rule: Under the actual-cost definition, fees may not under most circumstances include the labor costs of the employees who make the copies; a special service charge for extensive clerical or supervisory assistance must be reasonable and based on actual labor costs and cannot be charged to recover time spent examining or removing confidential information from records.
new_rules.trigger: Agency considers a labor component in a copy fee
new_rules.is_paraphrase: "Actual cost" is defined as "direct, chargeable costs related to the reproduction of a public record as determined by generally accepted accounting principles." The law does not give examples of actual costs but it does say that actual cost may not include costs the agency would have incurred if the copy request had not been made. This means that under most circumstances, fees may not include the labor costs of the agency employees who make the copies. However, if making the copies involves extensive clerical or supervisory assistance, the agency may charge a special service fee in addition to actual duplication costs. This service charge must be reasonable and based on actual labor costs but cannot be charged to recover fees for time spent examining or removing confidential information from records. Agencies also may charge to recover the costs of mailing copies. Complaints or disputes about all records copying fees may be directed to the State Chief Information Officer or their designee for mediation.
new_rules.source_type: N.C. Attorney General, North Carolina Open Government Guide (2019), 'Charging Fees', p. 20
new_rules.official_link: Current as posted (2019 edition, Attorney General Josh Stein / N.C. Press Association; guidance, not law; predates the Jan. 2025 change of Attorney General — no later edition located)
new_rules.amends: Guidance restating § 132-6.2(b) and § 132-6(c); adds the express statement that review/redaction time is never recoverable through the special service charge. Guide co-authored with the N.C. Press Association and published by NCDOJ.

new_rules.legal_concept: AG guidance: recovery of mailing costs
new_rules.atomic_rule: Agencies may charge to recover the costs of mailing copies.
new_rules.is_paraphrase: Agencies also may charge to recover the costs of mailing copies.
new_rules.source_type: N.C. Attorney General, North Carolina Open Government Guide (2019), 'Charging Fees', p. 20
new_rules.official_link: Current as posted (2019 edition, Attorney General Josh Stein / N.C. Press Association; guidance, not law; predates the Jan. 2025 change of Attorney General — no later edition located)
new_rules.amends: Guidance only — the statute's 'actual cost' is tied to 'reproduction'; postage recovery rests on the AG's reading. No handling fee addressed.

new_rules.legal_concept: Local government may accept electronic payment and pass through processing charges
new_rules.atomic_rule: A unit of local government may accept electronic payment (as defined in G.S. 147-86.20) in lieu of cash or check for any fee, charge or other receivable owed to it, may pay the card/merchant processing charges as a condition of accepting electronic payment, and may impose that charge as a surcharge on the person paying electronically.
new_rules.trigger: City chooses to accept electronic payment for a records fee
new_rules.is_paraphrase: A unit of local government, public hospital, or public authority may, in lieu of payment by cash or check, accept payment by electronic payment as defined in G.S. 147-86.20 for any tax, assessment, rate, fee, charge, rent, interest, penalty, or other receivable owed to it. A unit of local government, public hospital, or public authority may pay any negotiated discount, processing fee, transaction fee, or other charge imposed by a credit card, charge card, or debit card company, or by a third-party merchant bank, as a condition of contracting for the unit's or the authority's acceptance of electronic payment. A unit of local government, public hospital, or public authority may impose the fee or charge as a surcharge on the amount paid by the person using electronic payment.
new_rules.official_link: Current (ncleg.gov current through S.L. 2026-30; enacted S.L. 1999-434 s. 5, unamended)
new_rules.amends: Local Government Finance Act permission (not a public-records statute); cities are 'units of local government' (G.S. 159-7). Optional; convenience surcharge permitted.

new_rules.legal_concept: Governor's Cabinet-agency guidance: 5 cents/page recommended; no fee for electronic production or inspection
new_rules.atomic_rule: For State Cabinet agencies, no fee may be charged for inspecting public records or for records produced electronically; a nominal copying fee may be charged for printed copies — five cents per page is recommended — but no fee may exceed the actual cost of making the copies.
new_rules.related_rule_ids: recommended: $0.05/page printed; ceiling: actual cost; electronic: no fee
new_rules.is_paraphrase: Assessing Cost. No fees may be charged for inspecting public records or records produced electronically. Agencies may charge a nominal copying fee for records produced in printed format. Five cents per page is recommended, but no fee charged should exceed the actual cost of making the copies.
new_rules.source_type: Office of Governor Roy Cooper, 'Guidance for Public Records and Meetings Access for North Carolina State Government Employees' (July 2018), p. 2
new_rules.official_link: Current as posted (July 2018, Office of Governor Roy Cooper; guidance for Cabinet agencies, not law; predates the Jan. 2025 change of Governor — no later edition located)

new_rules.legal_concept: AG best practice: written acknowledgment with timetable and cost information
new_rules.atomic_rule: As a best practice (advisory), the agency should notify the requester in writing that the request was received, give a reasonable timetable, and — if fees might be charged — include information about those costs.
new_rules.trigger: Request received for which fees might be charged
new_rules.is_paraphrase: As a best practice, notify the requesting party in writing that the request has been received and give a reasonable timetable for a response. If this is a request for which fees might be charged, include information about those costs, but check with your agency's public records staff to make sure it is charging that kind of fee.

new_rules.legal_concept: No fee for inspection of public records
new_rules.atomic_rule: Government agencies may not charge fees for inspecting public records.
new_rules.trigger: Requester inspects rather than obtains copies
new_rules.is_paraphrase: May an agency charge fees for inspecting public records? Government agencies may not charge fees for inspecting public records.

applicability_notes: Chapter 132 applies to 'every public office, public officer or official (State or local, elected or appointed) ... or other unit of government of the State or of any county, unit, special district or other political subdivision of government' (§ 132-1(a)) — every § 132-6.2 figure/standard binds municipalities and state agencies alike (all_public_bodies).

North Carolina has NO uniform state-agency fee schedule and no NCAC title on public-records fees; individual state agencies adopt their own NCAC fee rules (e.g., NCAOC $0.25/page policy; State Ethics Commission; Commissioner of Banks) — none binds cities and none was extracted.

Governor's Office July 2018 guidance (five cents/page recommended; no fee for electronic production or inspection) is addressed to Cabinet-level employees and commissions — state_agencies_only; recorded as NC-9010 for the agency-regime note.
§ 132-1.4A(l) (recording copy fee ≤ actual cost) binds any 'law enforcement agency' — municipal police included.
§ 132-10 (GIS copies at reasonable cost; written no-commercial-use condition) is expressly county/city-specific — municipalities.
§ 159-32.1 (electronic payment) is a Local Government Finance Act permission for 'units of local government' incl. cities — municipalities (also counties, public authorities, hospitals).

AG 2019 Open Government Guide is official guidance addressed to all agencies; where it goes beyond statute (postage recovery; express no-fee-for-inspection; redaction time never recoverable) it is recorded as Official Guidance, not law.
material_negatives: No per-page copy rate, no color/oversized/specialty rate, no graduated bands, no free-page allowance for municipalities — everything hangs on the § 132-6.2(b) actual-cost ceiling.

No hourly labor rate, overhead %, billing increment, free-hours or periodic free-time allowance; labor is chargeable only as the 'reasonable' special service charge when a request requires 'extensive' IT resources or 'extensive' clerical/supervisory assistance ('extensive' undefined).
Review/redaction labor is categorically non-chargeable (§ 132-6(c); AG Guide).
No estimate/cost-notice threshold, requester response window, revision %, or estimate validity period; the AG Guide's cost-information-in-acknowledgment is advisory only.
No deposit or prepayment provision, no deposit cap, no nonpayment-withdrawal rule, no overrun re-issue rule; only § 132-6(a) 'upon payment of any fees' (pay-for-copies gate).
No dollar maximum, de-minimis, or minimum fee.
No municipal certification-fee statute located (delegated to 'law' by § 132-6.2(b) — unresolved).
No commercial-purpose surcharge; purpose may not be required (§ 132-6(b)); only the GIS-specific written no-commercial-use condition (§ 132-10).
No fee-waiver criteria, mandatory waiver, written-denial or waiver-appeal rule; only CIO mediation for 'unfair or unreasonable' fees; no forfeiture; no repeat/aggregation rule.
